rows.title: Liberals' 2026 budget passes in House of Commons
rows.summary: MPs voted 162 to 151 to pass the federal government's 2026 budget, which was tabled on Nov. 5. The Liberals now hold a majority of Commons seats after byelections and floor-crossings, so the vote was far less dramatic than last year's narrow budget vote. The budget relies on billions of dollars in new borrowing, mainly for infrastructure and other capital projects, and includes a $36-billion 'productivity mega-deduction' to encourage business investment and a top-up to the Groceries and Essentials Benefit. Opposition leaders attacked the scale of the borrowing, and the Parliamentary Budget Officer found Ottawa only narrowly on track to meet its own fiscal anchors. The budget still needs implementation bills before its measures become law.
rows.fact: The House of Commons passed Budget 2026 by 162 votes to 151 on Nov. 19 (Ottawa time). The budget pairs large new borrowing with tax measures, including a $36-billion productivity deduction for businesses and a top-up to a grocery benefit for lower-income households.
rows.outlook: The government must still table implementation bills, which will go through committee study and could be amended before the measures take effect.
rows.why: 정부가 빚을 내서 투자해 미래 성장을 이끌 수 있는지, 아니면 이자 부담만 키우는지를 실제 국가 예산을 통해 생각해 볼 수 있는 좋은 사례입니다.
rows.why_en: It is a real-world case for asking whether government borrowing to invest can drive future growth, or whether it mainly adds to interest costs.
rows.term_def: A rule a government sets for itself to keep its finances under control, such as keeping debt falling as a share of the economy. It signals to markets and voters that borrowing won't spiral.
rows.note: Vote held Nov. 19 ET (published 08:47 KST Nov. 20). Main budget measures (e.g. the $36B deduction) independently confirmed by the C.D. Howe memo; the 162-151 count is from the CP report. Distinct from the PBO borrowing warning covered Nov. 18.

opinion.title: Ottawa's Budget is Bold, Too Big, and Unfinished
opinion.author: Duncan Munn
opinion.summary: Munn, a former C.D. Howe Institute president, argues that Budget 2026 contains bold ideas but tries to fund too many priorities at once. He points to a projected deficit of about $62.3 billion, program spending up 8.9% in a year, and federal interest costs that now exceed health transfers to the provinces. He notes that roughly $158 billion in extra revenue over five years has been almost fully spent rather than saved as a buffer for the next shock. He praises the productivity deduction, which roughly halves the effective tax rate on new investment, and banking-competition reforms such as raising deposit insurance to $250,000. Overall, he calls for broad tax reform and less government-directed industrial policy instead of more spending.
opinion.why: 같은 예산을 두고 '투자 확대는 좋지만 지출이 너무 많다'는 전문가의 균형 잡힌 평가를 통해 재정 정책의 장단점을 함께 볼 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: It gives a balanced expert view of the same budget, praising its pro-investment measures while warning about overspending, so readers can weigh the trade-offs of fiscal policy.

rows.title: Number of people seeking unemployment aid ticks higher yet still low historically
rows.summary: The Labor Department reported that initial applications for unemployment benefits rose slightly to 203,000 in the week ending Nov. 14, up from a revised 202,000 the week before and above forecasts of about 197,000. The four-week average, which smooths out weekly swings, rose by 2,000 to 197,750. Claims have stayed below 220,000 all year, a historically low level suggesting most companies are keeping their workers. Hiring is still slow, though, in what economists call a 'low-hire, low-fire' job market, which makes it hard for young people and other new job seekers to find a first job. With 165,000 jobs added in October and unemployment at 4.1%, the Fed may see the labor market as strong enough to justify a December rate hike.
rows.fact: Initial jobless claims rose by 1,000 to 203,000 for the week ending Nov. 14, and the four-week average rose to 197,750. Reuters reported that continuing claims jumped 70,000 to 1.763 million, the highest since late August.
rows.outlook: Financial markets have priced in a quarter-point Fed rate increase at the December meeting, according to Reuters.
rows.why: 해고는 적지만 채용도 적은 '저채용·저해고' 노동시장은 곧 사회에 나갈 청년들이 첫 일자리를 구하기 어렵다는 뜻이고, 연준의 12월 금리 결정에도 영향을 주기 때문에 중요합니다.
rows.why_en: A 'low-hire, low-fire' job market means young people about to enter the workforce may struggle to land a first job, and the data also feeds into the Fed's December rate decision.
rows.term_def: The number of people who file for unemployment benefits for the first time in a given week; a fast, weekly signal of how many workers are being laid off.
rows.note: Official Labor Department data released Nov. 19, 8:30 a.m. ET (22:30 KST). Forecast, continuing-claims and rate-pricing figures cross-checked against the Reuters report (Lucia Mutikani) republished by KFGO.

opinion.title: The 'low hire, low fire' job market could finally crack in 2027
opinion.author: Kerry Hannon
opinion.summary: Columnist Kerry Hannon examines the same 'low-hire, low-fire' labor market using a Nov. 18 report from Indeed Hiring Lab and Glassdoor Economic Research. Job postings are above pre-pandemic levels in 299 of 385 US metro areas, but the gains are small. Postings for senior roles are rising while entry-level and mid-level postings are falling. Workers rate their pay and benefits at the lowest level since 2017 and wages are not keeping up with inflation, so many want to quit but have had few chances. The researchers expect job-hopping could return in 2027, but warn that a big market drop could stall the recovery.
opinion.why: 신입·중간급 채용 공고가 줄고 있다는 분석은 곧 진로를 정할 고3 학생들이 앞으로의 취업 시장을 이해하는 데 직접 도움이 됩니다.
opinion.why_en: Its finding that entry-level and mid-level job postings are shrinking speaks directly to seniors planning their future careers.

rows.title: Producer prices drop in Oct. on lower food prices
rows.summary: Bank of Korea data released on Nov. 20 show that South Korea's producer price index (PPI) fell 0.1% in October from September, its first monthly drop in three months. Farm, livestock and fishery prices fell 8.3% as good weather brought more fruit to market, with apples down about 29%, and pork demand eased after the Chuseok holiday. Other prices kept rising: industrial goods such as petroleum and chemical products rose 0.3%, utilities 0.2%, and the domestic supply price index, which includes import prices, 0.7%. From a year earlier, producer prices were still up 7.2% (7.6% in September). That means price pressure at the factory and wholesale level stays high and could feed into consumer prices later.
rows.fact: The PPI fell 0.1% month-on-month in October 2026 and was up 7.2% year-on-year. Cheaper farm, livestock and fishery goods (-8.3%) caused the drop, while industrial products (+0.3%) and utilities (+0.2%) kept rising.
rows.why: 생산자물가는 기업이 물건을 만들고 파는 단계의 가격이라 몇 달 뒤 우리가 마트와 식당에서 내는 소비자물가의 방향을 미리 보여 주는 신호이기 때문입니다.
rows.why_en: Producer prices are what businesses charge when they make and sell goods, so they give an early hint of where the prices you pay at stores and restaurants will go in the coming months.
rows.term_def: A measure of how the prices domestic producers charge for goods and services change over time, tracked at the factory or wholesale stage before goods reach shoppers; it often moves ahead of consumer prices.
rows.note: Bank of Korea release of Nov. 20 KST; figures cross-checked against Korea JoongAng Daily's copy of the Yonhap story and Seoul Economic Daily.

opinion.title: Producer prices fall for the first time in three months, but rise 0.2% excluding farm and fishery goods
opinion.author: Kim Hye-ran
opinion.summary: This analysis argues that October's small PPI decline hides continued price pressure: without the temporary plunge in farm and fishery goods, producer prices would have risen about 0.2% for the month. Earlier increases in raw material costs are reaching manufactured goods with a delay, with chemicals up 1.5%, petroleum products 1.9% and semiconductors 3.4% (DRAM +5.7%). Imported raw materials jumped 10.8%, which the BOK linked to September's oil price rise and October exchange-rate moves. For November, the BOK expects oil prices about 15% lower to pull producer prices down, while higher industrial city gas rates and airline fuel surcharges push them up. A BOK official called the farm-price drop largely temporary.
opinion.why: 겉으로 보이는 '물가 하락' 숫자만 보지 말고, 일시적인 요인을 빼면 가격 압력이 여전히 남아 있는지 따져 보는 법을 배울 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: It teaches you to look past a headline 'prices fell' number and ask whether price pressure remains once temporary factors are stripped out.

rows.title: UK borrowing below forecasts as Healey's deficit picture improves
rows.summary: Official data published on Nov. 20 showed the UK government borrowed £17.0 billion in October, slightly less than the £18.0 billion economists expected, and borrowing for April to September was revised down by £3.6 billion thanks to stronger tax receipts and faster third-quarter growth. Interest payments on government debt reached £11.2 billion, the highest October on record and about a third more than a year earlier, partly because payments on inflation-linked bonds rise with inflation. Over the first seven months of the 2026/27 fiscal year, borrowing was £111.3 billion, £7.3 billion less than a year earlier but £3.3 billion above the Office for Budget Responsibility's March forecast. Britain has the highest borrowing costs in the G7, and money spent on interest cannot go to public services. The figures leave Chancellor John Healey little room for new spending or tax cuts.
rows.fact: UK public sector net borrowing was £17.0bn in October 2026, against a Reuters poll median of £18.0bn. Debt interest was a record £11.2bn for an October, and year-to-date borrowing was £111.3bn, down £7.3bn on a year earlier.
rows.outlook: An ICAEW economist said rising inflation, higher interest rates and a possible Bank of England rate rise in December are bound to push up the cost of government borrowing.
rows.why: 정부가 빚에 대한 이자로 쓰는 돈이 늘어나면 교육·의료 같은 공공서비스에 쓸 돈이 줄어들기 때문에, 금리와 물가가 나라 살림에 어떤 영향을 주는지 보여주는 좋은 사례입니다.
rows.why_en: When a government spends more on interest on its debt, it has less for schools and hospitals, so this is a clear example of how interest rates and inflation affect a country's budget.
rows.term_def: The money a government pays each year to investors who lent it money by buying its bonds; it rises when interest rates go up, or, for inflation-linked bonds, when inflation goes up.
rows.note: ONS public sector finances for October, released Nov. 20 (07:00 UK). Figures cross-checked against ITV News's report of the same release. No readable editorial on the release was found, so C is an analysis piece on the same topic.

opinion.title: Chart of the week: debt on the rise
opinion.outlet: ICAEW Insights (Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales)
opinion.author: ICAEW Insights
opinion.summary: The ICAEW analysis notes that UK public sector net debt passed £3 trillion for the first time in September 2026, about 94% of GDP, with the past five years seeing the biggest increase, around £768bn. It names four main causes: years of deficits, the 2008-09 bank rescues, pandemic spending, and energy-bill support in 2021-23. Debt is near its highest share of GDP since the 1960s, and high interest rates have made it much more expensive to service, especially as the population ages. It points out that Britain took 316 years to reach £1tn of debt but only six years to go from £2tn to £3tn. It projects about £3.5tn by 2030 and £4tn around 2036, sooner if new shocks hit.
opinion.why: 이번 10월 이자 비용 사상 최고치가 왜 나왔는지, 즉 수십 년간 쌓인 나랏빚과 높은 금리가 어떻게 맞물려 있는지 큰 그림으로 이해할 수 있게 해줍니다.
opinion.why_en: It gives the big picture behind October's record interest bill, showing how decades of accumulated government debt and today's high interest rates combine to squeeze the budget.

rows.title: Japan's core inflation accelerates in October, cementing rate hike expectations
rows.summary: Japan's core consumer prices, which leave out fresh food, rose 2.2% in October from a year earlier, up from 2.1% in September but a little below the 2.3% forecast, staying above the Bank of Japan's 2% target for a second month. Goods prices rose 3.2% while services rose only 1.4%, so the pressure is coming mostly from costly imported fuel and raw materials, pushed up by the weak yen and the Middle East war, rather than from wages. The BOJ already raised its policy rate to 1.25% in September, and the data strengthens expectations of a further hike to 1.5% at its December 17-18 meeting. Critics warn that Japan's surprise third-quarter contraction and recent market turmoil could make the central bank pause.
rows.fact: Japan's October core CPI (excluding fresh food) rose 2.2% year on year, up from 2.1% in September, against a 2.3% median forecast. The BOJ's preferred gauge, which also excludes fuel, slowed to 2.2% from 2.4%, and food inflation eased to 2.2% from 2.9%.
rows.outlook: Most analysts polled by Reuters expect the BOJ to hike in December and again by end-March, though some warn unstable markets could make it hold.
rows.why: 일본이 금리를 올리면 엔화 가치와 국제 자금 흐름이 바뀌어, 일본과 경쟁하며 교역하는 한국의 수출 가격 경쟁력과 금융시장에도 영향을 줄 수 있습니다.
rows.why_en: If Japan raises interest rates, the yen's value and global money flows could shift, affecting the export competitiveness and financial markets of Korea, which competes and trades closely with Japan.
rows.term_def: A consumer price measure that leaves out items whose prices swing a lot, such as fresh food in Japan, to show the underlying price trend that central banks watch when setting interest rates.
rows.note: Released Nov. 20 KST; core figures confirmed in a shorter Reuters wire copy. Distinct from Japan's Q3 GDP and October exports covered earlier this week.

opinion.title: Japan October-26 CPI Inflation Report
opinion.author: Gianluca Benigno
opinion.summary: Economist Gianluca Benigno breaks down the October data: headline CPI rose 2.3% (below the 2.5% forecast), core rose 2.2% to its highest since December 2025, and the core-core measure eased to 2.2%. He argues the slowdown in core-core mostly reflects a base effect, because food prices jumped a lot a year earlier, and that underlying inflation is holding near 2.2%, driven by goods prices and rising hotel prices. He notes energy prices rose as government subsidies shrank, while rice prices fell nearly 30%. His base case is a BOJ hike to 1.50% on December 18. That could slip to January if Governor Ueda sounds cautious on November 30 or the December Tankan survey is weak.
opinion.why: 같은 물가 지표라도 무엇이 가격을 끌어올리는지에 따라 중앙은행의 금리 판단이 달라진다는 점을 보여 줍니다.
opinion.why_en: It shows that even with the same inflation number, what is driving prices up can change a central bank's interest-rate decision.
